about.title: Personal Injury Help in Torrance, California
about.longDescription: Torrance sits at the southern edge of Los Angeles County, and a lot of traffic moves through it. Hawthorne Boulevard carries shoppers and commuters north to south, Crenshaw Boulevard runs parallel to the east, Pacific Coast Highway cuts across the bottom of the city, and the I-405 San Diego Freeway pulls in drivers from across the South Bay. In 2025, the most recent final crash year on record, Torrance logged 329 injury collisions. Those crashes hurt 490 people and took 5 lives. Public records also show reports tend to peak on Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m., when the work week is winding down and the roads fill up. If one of those numbers is now your story, here is what we do. We handle personal injury claims in Torrance and throughout Los Angeles County. There is no charge to reach out, and we work on contingency, which means no fee unless there is a recovery. You describe what happened, and our team will evaluate your claim and help you move forward.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Torrance Claim

items.title: The clock runs for two years — usually
items.desc: California gives most injury claims a two-year filing window from the date of the injury. If a city or state entity is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so timing matters more than people expect.

items.title: Partly at fault? You can still recover
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault. Your share of blame reduces what you recover, but it does not shut the door on your claim.

items.title: No cap on pain-and-suffering damages
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no dollar limit on non-economic damages such as pain, lost sleep, or the toll on your daily life. Those losses count.

items.title: You pay nothing unless there is a recovery
items.desc: We work on contingency. Our fee comes out of a recovery, and if there is none, you do not owe attorney fees.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to happen in Torrance?
items.answer: According to public collision records, the corridors with the highest counts in Torrance are Hawthorne Boulevard, the I-405 San Diego Freeway, Crenshaw Boulevard, and Pacific Coast Highway. These are neutral counts that largely track where traffic volume is heaviest, not a judgment about any particular road. Records also show reported crashes tend to peak on Fridays between 3 and 5 p.m.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim in California?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims, California allows two years from the date of the injury. If your claim involves a government entity — a city vehicle or a public property hazard, for example — the deadline can be as short as six months. Speaking with our team early helps you avoid missing either one.

items.question: What if the crash was partly my fault?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, so you are not barred from recovering just because you share some blame. Your recovery is reduced by your percentage of fault. Our team can help sort out how fault is likely to be assigned.

items.question: What does it cost to get a case review?
items.answer: Nothing. Our initial consultation is free, and we work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. You will not receive a bill from us at any point.
